newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says U.S. delays granting phone licence.
newsitem.headline: NTT says U.S. delays granting phone licence.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said on Wednesday that the U.S. Federal Communications Commission had informed NTT's U.S. unit that the granting of a U.S. licence to provide international phone services would be delayed.

NTT said in late January that its wholly owned U.S. unit -- NTT America Inc -- had applied to the FCC for a licence to operate telecommunications services between the United States and other countries besides Japan.

Analysts at the time expressed scepticism about the possibility of quick U.S. approval. Some Japanese media reports on Wednesday attributed the delay to U.S. irritation with Japan's decision to keep a 20 percent ceiling on foreign investment in NTT and overseas carrier Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD).
KDD also said on Wednesday that the FCC had delayed approval of its application for a U.S. licence to provide international phone services.

A KDD spokesman said the FCC had informed its U.S. unit that the U.S. Trade Representative, the U.S. Department of Commerce and the U.S. State Department had requested that KDD be excluded from a simplified application procedure under which companies seeking U.S. phone licences would be automatically granted permission within 35 days of making an application.
